messages:
ops-bot: [INCIDENT CREATED] 1719994321 - ALERT: continuous-batcher queue growth detected on cluster-us-east-1. p95 /v1/generate > 3s, multiple nodes reporting OOM/KV-cache paging. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

ops-bot: severity=P2; affected_shards=3; symptom=latency spike + OOMs; runbook=continuous-batcher-paging. Please ack.

marta: ack I'm oncall. seeing repeated container restarts on batcher pods, pod status OOMKilled. stack shows CUDA OOMs and illegal address in launcher.

marta: logs excerpt:
```
launcher: Allocation failed: "CUDA out of memory" at cublas_gemm:245
runtime: cuda error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
kernel: page fault on encrypted memory region, vm_fault_killable
kubelet: container not healthy, last state: OOMKilled
```

raj: jumping in. likely a runaway batch growth + KV prefetch tipping memory. We've seen similar when prefetch+continuous-batch accumulate stale KV caches.

sam: customer-sre here. Is there active customer impact? CS systems show elevated 5xx and timeouts to a subset of traffic hitting small-model and xl-model routes. Leah are any tickets open?

leah: customer-success-bot: two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, BrightHealth) reported timeouts. Acme reported 20% of requests >5s since ~1719994200. I've drafted a short status message for them.

marta: mitigation plan (quick):
1) throttle continuous batching: set batching.max_batch_size=8 and batching.max_concurrent=8 (from 64)
2) disable KV prefetch on affected model variant (prefetch.enabled=false)
3) route high-latency traffic to fallback model variant (model: gpt-open-lite)
4) cordon + drain one flapping node to clear paging pressure

raj: agree. do steps 1-3 via runtime config ASAP, then do node drains if queue doesn't come down. I'll prepare the k8s patches.

marta: applying runtime patch now. curl command:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/admin/batching-config" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"model": "gpt-xl-prod", "batching": {"max_batch_size": 8, "max_concurrent": 8, "prefetch": {"enabled": false}}}'
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: config-change accepted, rollout started to runtime-config service (3/3 replicas).

marta: pushed routing change to send 10% traffic to gpt-open-lite as emergency fallback: `route weight gpt-xl-prod->gpt-open-lite 10%`

sam: I'm starting cordon/drain on node us-east-1a-n02 (most flappy). command: `kubectl cordon us-east-1a-n02 && kubectl drain us-east-1a-n02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

raj: watching metrics: batch_queue_length for gpt-xl-prod peaked at 18k -> currently 2.1k after throttle. p95 latency dropped from 3.2s -> 720ms. memory pressure still high on node us-east-1a-n03.

marta: container restarts are down from 15/min -> 1/min. CUDA OOM errors still in a few pods. I'm going to restart batcher on pods showing illegal address to clear corrupted KV caches: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher-gpt-xl-prod --namespace inference` (one at a time).

leah: CS update sent: "We are actively mitigating elevated latency caused by backend batcher instability. We have enacted throttles, diverted a portion of traffic, and are rebalancing nodes. Expect progressive improvement over next 15-30 minutes." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident note added: mitigation in progress. next update requested in 10 minutes.

raj: after restarts, KV-cache growth no longer climbs; p95 at 390ms on gpt-xl-prod in the last 2m. page-fault counts reduced to baseline. However, one node coredumped during drain with dmesg showing repeated GPU page fault and MIG driver reset. filing follow-up ticket for kernel/driver triage.

marta: agreed. immediate customer impact is reduced; keeping incident live for root-cause follow-up and driver/kernel ticket. Assigning follow-up to @raj for postmortem.

sam: handing ops to @raj for next shift. I'll monitor CS escalation channel for any regressions.

raj: ack taking follow-up. I'll collect heap dumps, KV cache metrics, and host dmesg. plan: repro with synthetic load in staging using prefetch on to validate prefetch bug, then propose fix (limit prefetch cache size + defensive OOM throttling).

leah: customers notified of remediation and we offered to run a private test with their workload if they'd like.

marta: final note before handoff: incident status: mitigated -> partial service degradation still possible but stable. root cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher + KV prefetch + edge case in driver leads to runaway memory growth + page faults under certain sequence lengths. follow-up: rollback prefetch default until patched, add runtime guard rails to throttle prefetch growth.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: mitigated -> monitoring. incident closed window scheduled: 1719996121.

raj: handing oncall to duty rotation later today. will file postmortem template and tag infra/driver/eng-runtime teams.

customer-success-bot: Logged CS tickets and updated SLA tracker.

marta: thanks team, closing comms here. if anyone sees fresh OOMs reopen thread.
